title: add paired-permutation-eval-gate-and-per-prompt-fault-localizer
author: Asha Patel
description:
Motivation: Existing evaluation gates rely heavily on bootstrap intervals and cohort-level aggregates which can mask paired differences on small prompt-sets and make root-cause triage noisy. This PR introduces a paired-permutation significance gate that operates on per-example paired deltas between baseline and candidate, combined with an FDR-controlled per-prompt fault localizer that surfaces which prompts drive the regression signal. The gate is lightweight, deterministic (seeded permutation), and designed to be cheap for CI (default 2000 permutations with early stopping).

What this change does (summary):
- Adds a new CI hook `permutation_paired_gate` that computes a paired-permutation p-value for the mean delta and fails the CI when p < alpha (alpha default 0.01). The gate supports one-sided and two-sided tests and a configurable effect-size guard (Cohen's d).
- Implements a per-prompt fault localizer that ranks prompts by their paired contribution and reports the top-K problematic prompts with summary stats and small example diffs to aid reviewers. Localizer applies Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction across prompts to control false positives.
- Integrates the gate into the existing eval orchestration pipeline and adds a lightweight CLI `evalctl gate-run` option to run only the permutation gate locally for debugging.
- Adds unit and integration tests, and a short docs page describing usage, configuration knobs, and rollout guidance.

Checklist: 
- [x] API for paired-permutation test and effect-size guard
- [x] CI hook and config template for repo-level inclusion
- [x] Fault localizer reporter + JSON artifact output for triage UI
- [x] Tests: unit (permutation math), e2e (small synthetic prompt set), CLI smoke
- [x] Docs + migration notes

Implementation notes (details):
- New core routines live in `eval_harness/stat_tests/permutation.py`. We implemented a vectorized permutation routine with early stopping when running mean-of-deltas crosses the critical threshold in more than (1-alpha) fraction of permutations. The implementation uses numpy for speed and explicitly avoids resampling with replacement (we do label-swapping of paired differences).
- The gate wraps the core test in `ci/hooks/permutation_gate.py` and emits two artifacts on failure: (1) `permutation_summary.json` with p-value, observed_mean_delta, effect_size, permutation_trace (sampled quantiles) and (2) `prompt_localizer.json` listing top-20 prompts and per-prompt p-values and corrected flags. The artifacts are intentionally compact to keep CI upload costs low.
- The localizer ranks prompts by absolute paired-delta and computes a per-prompt paired sign test; we then apply Benjamini-Hochberg across all prompts in the set. For small prompt-sets (<30) we fall back to an exact sign test.
- Default permutation count is 2000; for heavy workloads CI config allows lowering to 500 for faster feedback. There is an env var `EVAL_PERM_SEED` to ensure reproducible runs in CI.

Testing and validation: 
- Unit tests cover the permutation engine with deterministic seeds and edge cases (zero-variance prompts, constant deltas).
- e2e integration uses a synthetic prompt-set where we inject known per-prompt regressions; the gate triggers and the localizer lists the injected prompts in the top-3 ranking in 97/100 runs.
- Performance: a 500-prompt paired run with 2000 permutations completes in ~18s on CI's standard runner; we added a micro-benchmark in `tests/bench/test_permutation_bench.py`.

Rollout plan: 
- Stage 1 (canary): enable gate as non-blocking in `eval-harness` repo for two weeks with notifications to #eval-alerts; collect artifacts for false-positive analysis.
- Stage 2: after tuning thresholds and verifying low false-positive rate, flip gate to blocking for PRs that touch `models/` or `infra/` changes.

Migration notes: existing regression gates are unaffected. To opt-in to the permutation gate add a small config snippet to `eval_config.yaml` (example in docs). The gate emits artifacts compatible with the triage UI; product infra already supports the artifact schema.

Related: ENG-2134 (evaluate alternative paired tests), ENG-2178 (CI gating roadmap).
